about: Annual community events by place type (size band). Read by the community calendar; decides no outcome by itself. Every row is SOURCED (quote from a fetched page) or ESTIMATED (basis and spread). Town-specific festivals are a later part.

placeTypes.basis: Census urban-area cutoff of 2,500; spread checked against the share of places each band holds.
Band where one high school and one fairground usually serve the whole place; spread 8,000 to 20,000.
Band of one to a few high schools; spread 40,000 to 100,000.
Band of many neighborhoods each holding its own events; spread 250,000 to 500,000.

events.name: Fourth of July parade and fireworks
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: Wikipedia, Independence Day (United States), fetched 2026-11-11: "Parades are often attended in many towns and cities" and "Towns of all sizes hold celebrations."

events.name: High school homecoming game, parade and dance
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: Wikipedia, Homecoming, fetched 2026-11-11: held "usually in late September or early October"; "A dance commonly follows the game"; many celebrations include "a parade featuring the school's choir, marching band and sports teams."

events.name: County or regional fair
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: Wikipedia pages on agricultural shows and county fairs, fetched 2026-11-11, give no US season, length or count (they say only that these are the North American terms for agricultural shows), so the late-summer season and about six days are estimates from the common US fair calendar; spread: start any time from June to September, three to ten days. A researcher turns this to SOURCED from state fair association calendars.

events.name: Fall harvest or heritage festival
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: Wikipedia, Harvest festival, fetched 2026-11-11, gives no North American date (only the Pilgrims' 1621 harvest thanksgiving), so the autumn season is an estimate; spread: September through November, one to three days.

events.name: Holiday parade and tree lighting
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: Wikipedia, Christmas parade, fetched 2026-11-11, shows parades held on or just after Thanksgiving (Philadelphia on the day, Peoria the day after); tree lightings are not covered, so the window is an estimate; spread: the weekend after Thanksgiving to the second week of December.

events.name: School play or concert
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: No page fetched; ESTIMATED from the school year (fall term and spring term) with a spread of one to three performances a year per school.

events.name: Church supper or club meeting
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: No page fetched; ESTIMATED as one gathering a month; spread: monthly to quarterly.

events.name: Neighborhood festival or block party
events.scaleMeaning: ESTIMATED share of residents who attend; spread 0.5x to 2x.
events.source: No page fetched; ESTIMATED as warm-season weekends in places large enough to hold many neighborhoods; spread: May to October.
